primitives.name: Closing Line Value
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## TL;DR — the one insight that matters **Closing Line Value (CLV) is the only sharp-accepted benchmark of skill, and almost nobody in our competitive set publishes it.** Tout services sell win-rate.
primitives.assumptions: Market odds are fair, outcomes are binary, and CLV reflects true edge after de-vigging.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When CLV < 0, the bet is expected to lose; when CLV > 0, it is expected to win.

layer2.mapping: CLV is derived from de-vigged odds and model calibration, forming a kernel for edge validation in GSI.
layer2.telemetry: User CLV tracking, Brier score, and edge consistency metrics.

primitives.verbatim_quote: We already *compute* CLV, de-vig, calibration (Brier/ECE), and an agreement-gated edge engine in `packages/prediction-engine` — we just don't surface them yet.
primitives.assumptions: Vig is constant across books, and de-vigging removes book bias.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When vig is high, de-vigged probabilities become unreliable.

layer2.mapping: De-vigged odds form an isomorphic space to fair market expectations, enabling CLV computation in GSI.
layer2.telemetry: Fair line consistency, deviation from book lines.

primitives.name: Calibration Score
primitives.verbatim_quote: We already *compute* CLV, de-vig, calibration (Brier/ECE), and an agreement-gated edge engine in `packages/prediction-engine` — we just don't surface them yet.
primitives.assumptions: Predictions are probabilistic, and outcomes are observed.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Brier score approaches zero as predictions become perfectly calibrated.

layer2.mapping: Calibration scores underpin CLV validity by ensuring model reliability in GSI.
layer2.telemetry: Model reliability, ECE (Expected Calibration Error), and Brier score trends.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that CLV serves as a universal skill metric because it measures the difference between a model’s prediction and the book’s implied probability, adjusted for vigorish. This creates a sharp benchmark that avoids the noise of win rates and sample size manipulation. In GSI, CLV is computed via de-vigged odds and calibrated via Brier/ECE scores, forming a robust kernel for edge validation. GSE uses this kernel to transition states in real-time, updating user CLV and validating picks against market consensus. The failure mode of competitors lies in their reliance on win-rate or accuracy without CLV, leading to overfitting or misaligned incentives. The dual nature of CLV—both as a performance indicator and a strategic anchor—enables a principled approach to distinguishing honest tools from tout services.
